## Natural history notes

A medium-sized songbird characterized by its prominent crest, thick orange-red bill, and long tail, with males bright red overall and females warm brown with reddish highlights on the wings, tail, and crest. In Florida, it is common in shrubs, thickets, forest edges, hammocks, gardens, parks, yards, and other habitats with dense vegetation for cover and nesting. It feeds mainly on seeds, fruits, and insects, usually foraging in low vegetation or on the ground and often seen in pairs.
